Orange Island & Inter Contra

We are excited to announce our partnership with Inter Contra, a leading telecommunications infrastructure and solutions provider known for innovation, excellence, and strong industry expertise.

Through this partnership, Inter Contra will be bringing reliable network infrastructure to Orange Island, including telecommunications towers, wireless connectivity, and engineering support. This means residents can look forward to better network coverage, faster internet, and more dependable communication services for everyday living.

Inter Contra will also support the estate with telecommunications engineering and infrastructure services, helping to build a strong and future-ready network across the community.

Orange Island & Decentralized Energy Limited (DEL)

We are pleased to announce our partnership with Decentralized Energy Limited (DEL), a company committed to transforming how energy is delivered across Nigeria.

At DEL, the belief is simple, Nigeria does not lack energy; the challenge lies in the infrastructure and execution needed to make it accessible. Through this partnership, DEL will bring cleaner, more reliable, and affordable power solutions to Orange Island, ensuring residents enjoy uninterrupted energy for everyday living.

Driven by a mission to make consistent and sustainable power a reality across Nigeria and West Africa, DEL operates on strong principles that guide how every project is planned, built, and managed.

PRESS STATEMENT

Orange Island Announces Board and Management Transitions

Lagos, Nigeria —Orange Island Development Company today announces the
retirement of its Chairman, Alhaji Waheed Kassim from the Board, alongside the retirement from executive management of its pioneer CEO Director, Olayinka Ogunsulire and CFO, Olusegun Faloju.

These transitions mark the close of a formative chapter in Orange Island’s journey. Under their stewardship, Orange Island evolved from concept to a landmark development, setting new benchmarks for integrated, master-planned communities and establishing a strong foundation for long-term growth. While stepping back from executive roles, Ms. Ogunsulire and Mr. Faloju will continue to serve as members of the Board providing continuity and strategic perspective.

The Board expresses its deep appreciation to the retiring leaders for their vision, discipline and commitment, which have positioned Orange Island as a reference point for quality and innovation, in sustainable urban development.

Concurrently, the Board announces the appointment of Mr. Lookman Durosinmi-Etti as the new Chairman of the Board. Mr. Durosinmi-Etti, a sitting non-executive director of Orange Island Development Company, is Senior Partner and one of the founding forces behind the leading Nigerian legal practice Jackson, Etti & Edu. He has over three decades of proven expertise in commercial, real estate, and intellectual property law. His career spans leadership in multinational transactions, advisory roles on complex infrastructure and property projects across Africa, and recognised contributions in legal practice and business strategy.

He brings a strong commitment to governance excellence and sustainable development complementing Orange Island’s strategic ambitions.
The Board looks forward to Mr. Durosinmi-Etti’s leadership as it advances the Island’s next phase focused on scale, operational excellence, and value creation for residents and stakeholders.

Further announcements regarding executive leadership will be made in due course.

Orange Island Development Company Responds to Recent Media Coverage on Drainage Violations
Orange Island, Lagos — Tuesday, 15th July, 2025

Orange Island Development Company is aware of recent media reports that do not accurately reflect our operations. While we respect the media’s role in informing the public, we find it necessary to clarify these issues to prevent misunderstanding among stakeholders and the community.

For clarity, we wish to state the following:

  • Orange Island has no drainage channel violations whatsoever.
  • The stop-work order mentioned in the reports relates to an area adjoining the Lekki foreshore, adjacent to the Orange Island access road—not to Orange Island itself. The Commissioner and his team inspected this adjoining area on Friday, 11th July. 
  • Orange Island is a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) with the Lagos State Government, under the oversight of the Ministry of Waterfront Infrastructure Development and all relevant regulatory authorities. Dredging works for Orange Island were completed in 2016 in full compliance with statutory requirements.

We believe that accuracy, balance, and context are essential to fair reporting and remain committed to working constructively with the media to ensure future coverage is based on verified facts and reflects an accurate perspective.

For further information, or to request an interview or comment, please contact hello@orangeislandng.com.

Management
Orange Island Development Company

ORANGE ISLAND MANAGEMENT AND MAINTENANCE FEES
Orange Island encourages all subscribers to pay their facility management and facility maintenance fees to enable us fulfill our commitment to maintaining and enhancing the facilities, infrastructure, and services on the Island.

One off Facilities Management Fees – are paid by each property owner as a one-off fee which will be used to purchase all the vehicles, tools, equipment and machinery required to maintain all the facilities and utilities in the common areas.

Annual Maintenance Fees – are used for all the administration and operational costs annually, to maintain and service the CCTV system, the security post, all security personnel, maintenance and repairs of all infrastructures (street lights, drainages, roads, walkways, park areas, etc.), facilities staff, utilities (power, water, fire hydrants, sewage system etc.) operations, maintenance and repairs of these.

Please reach out to our team via phone or email if you have any further enquiries.

LAGOS STATE BUILDING PERMIT – WATERFRONT INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT CLEARANCE

We have just been informed by the Lagos State Ministry of Waterfront Infrastructure Development that ALL subscribers on Orange Island must obtain a Waterfront Infrastructure Development Clearance along with their Lagos State Building approval before commencing construction of their homes.

Subscribers currently awaiting approvals from Lagos State, in pre-construction and already occupied on the island are required to get their Waterfront Infrastructure Development Clearance within 7 days from the date of this notification.

Please see below the requirements for obtaining your Waterfront clearance:

  1. Certified true copies of title documents
  2. A set of architectural drawings
  3. A copy of Physical Planning Technical Report
  4. Application letter addressed to Honorable Commissioner for the Ministry of Waterfront Infrastructure Development, with your date, phone number and email
  5. Company’s form C02 & C07 (Corporate Organisations)
  6. Certificate of Incorporation (Corporate Organisations)
  7. Evidence of 3 (Three) years Tax Clearance

These documents are to be taken to Room 204, Block 10, Second Floor, Ministry of Waterfront Infrastructure Development. The Secretariat Alausa, Lagos for processing.
